|  ![nfpa1140wildlands.jpg](https://courses.suncrestcollege.ca/images/nfpa1140wildlands.jpg)  
 |  NFPA 1140 is the National Fire Protection Association’s consolidated standard for Wildland Fire Protection, created by combining four previous standards to improve clarity, consistency, and usability. This standard outlines the fundamental knowledge and skills required to safely and effectively combat wildland fires, with a strong emphasis on operations in the wildland–urban interface (WUI). The course introduces key concepts essential for wildland firefighting, including basic fire behavior, firefighter safety, methods of attack (such as backfiring and burnout operations), water and foam delivery systems, and air operations safety. Wildland incidents present significant risks to both firefighters and communities—particularly where homes and infrastructure border natural vegetation. NFPA 1140 equips firefighters with the critical skills and understanding needed to operate safely, protect property, and support effective wildfire suppression efforts. ***** **Minimum Enrollment Requirement** Please note that each course must meet a minimum number of participants to run. ### Blended Delivery 
This course will be delivered in a blended format, starting with self-paced online study on the user-friendly platform Brightspace and followed by in-person sessions. Delivering some theory and exam preparation online will allow more hands-on training (HOT) time and increased focus on mastery learning. The dates listed below represent the face-to-face portion of the course. The Self Study online portion will begin when registration closes and the minimum class size is met. Participants who successfully complete both the written examination and the practical skills evaluation will be awarded IFSAC certification.
